gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named-lab comparison of the candidates: the only sourced ones are RTINGS's side-by-side verdicts (Flow 2 'noticeably better build quality' and 'slightly more refined typing quality' than Keychron's K Max line; Air75 V3 3.5 mm travel against Keychron's 3.0 mm maximum), because RTINGS's measured figures were locked to members on 2026-11-21.
standout_why: Compared against RTINGS best low-profile (cited, rank 1), mechkeyfoundry's Air75 V3 vs Flow 2 vs K3 Max, and TechWise. The RTINGS best-of text carries no latency, travel, noise, height or weight figure. Mechkeyfoundry says 'every battery and travel figure here is the maker's rating', and TechWise attributes nothing to a lab. The measured figures sit on RTINGS's own review pages behind its membership lock, so what I could source is RTINGS's wording, not its numbers. RTINGS best-for-Mac (rank 2) and the Tom's Guide pages returned only navigation, so they were not compared.
decides: It confirms the pick rather than changing it. RTINGS names the NuPhy Air75 V3 its best low-profile keyboard, rates its single-key and multi-key latency 'excellent', and says it is 'fully compatible with both Windows and macOS'. The Lofree Flow 2 places on typing: RTINGS recommends it in its Typing and Office articles and puts its build and typing quality above Keychron's K Max line. RTINGS gives the Air75 V3 'slightly better gaming performance overall' and calls the Flow 2's VIA software 'relatively more limited'. One caution for the Flow 2: RTINGS's first unit had intermittent wired connection faults and was replaced.
